react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms — multi-database ORA (RaMP), m/z-direct network activity (Mummichog), and KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR) — converge on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant perturbed biological system. RaMP ORA reports KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at rank 2 with an FDR of 2.16×10⁻¹⁴ and a fold enrichment of 1250, driven by five input steroids. Mummichog confirms this pathway indirectly: rank 1 (p=0.0022) reports 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' and rank 2 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' with near-complete overlap (9–10 of 10 pathway members hit). MetaboAnalystR independently ranks KEGG:hsa00140 first (p=8.4×10⁻⁶), which corresponds to the same steroid hormone axis. RaMP further identifies Reactome R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (FDR 1.1×10⁻¹³) and WikiPathways WP496 'Steroid biosynthesis' (FDR 9.96×10⁻¹³). The five confirmed driver metabolites — testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estradiol (KEGG:C00951), dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), and dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227) — are present in every steroid pathway across all three paradigms. A secondary signal emerges around thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198): Mummichog ranks 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' at rank 3 (p=0.021) and 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' at rank 6 (p=0.052), indicating modest perturbation of the eicosanoid axis. Quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) and dehydroascorbic acid (KEGG:C05422) contribute to tryptophan and ascorbate metabolism hits respectively, but these are secondary to the overwhelmingly significant steroid hormone signature. The pattern is consistent with a treatment that either directly modulates steroidogenesis enzymes (e.g. aromatase, 17β-HSD) or alters upstream cholesterol flux toward sex steroid biosynthesis.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment paradigms converge on androgen and estrogen metabolism as the dominant perturbed biological system in this metabolomics comparison. RaMP ORA returns SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top-ranked SMPDB pathway with FDR = 2.16×10⁻¹⁴ and KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 2 with the same FDR, both driven by five input steroids from the differential set. WikiPathways WP:WP4523 (Classical pathway of steroidogenesis with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid metabolism) ranks 5 in RaMP (FDR = 2.65×10⁻¹⁴) and Reactome REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) ranks 6 (FDR = 1.10×10⁻¹³), extending the finding to the broader steroidogenesis hierarchy. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis confirms this finding with MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 0 (p = 0.0019) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 1 (p = 0.0028), both exhibiting near-complete pathway coverage from the steroid input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranks KEGG:hsa00140 at rank 0 with five steroid hits from the input set. The five driver steroids are testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, dehydroepiandrosterone, and dihydrotestosterone, each present as a confirmed hit across multiple orthogonal tools. Quinolinic acid independently maps to MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (p = 0.054) and KEGG:hsa00760 (Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism, MetaboAnalystR rank 2, p = 0.073), representing a secondary perturbed system.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment paradigms converge on androgen and estrogen metabolism as the dominant perturbed biological system in this metabolomics comparison. RaMP ORA returns SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top-ranked SMPDB pathway with FDR = 2.16×10⁻¹⁴ and KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 2 with the same FDR, both driven by five input steroids from the differential set. WikiPathways WP:WP4523 (Classical pathway of steroidogenesis with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid metabolism) ranks 5 in RaMP (FDR = 2.65×10⁻¹⁴) and Reactome REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) ranks 6 (FDR = 1.10×10⁻¹³), extending the finding to the broader steroidogenesis hierarchy. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis confirms this finding with MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 0 (p = 0.0019) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 1 (p = 0.0028), both exhibiting near-complete pathway coverage from the steroid input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranks KEGG:hsa00140 at rank 0 with five steroid hits from the input set. The five driver steroids are testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, dehydroepiandrosterone, and dihydrotestosterone, each present as a confirmed hit across multiple orthogonal tools. Quinolinic acid independently maps to MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (p = 0.054) and KEGG:hsa00760 (Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism, MetaboAnalystR rank 2, p = 0.073), representing a secondary perturbed system.
